newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares tick up, seen up, on U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares tick up, seen up, on U.S. holiday.

text.p: Russian shares firmed slightly on slow trading on Monday, a United States holiday, but traders saw the market ready for a pickup, though they disagreed on how fast the bull would charge.
Mosenergo closed at $0.98 on the Russian Trading System (RTS) after $0.9825 at Friday's close. Surgutnefegaz ticked up to $0.426 after $0.423 and UES firmed to $0.0836 after $0.0829.
Purneftegaz, which will stay in state-owned Rosneft's control after a court on Monday refused to return it to former owner holding company Sidanko, eased to $2.28 after $2.30.
The RTS Index gained 1.58 percent on $11.4 million trade.
Brunswick's Martin Diggle, who said Monday's low volumes and slow appreciation were due to the U.S. absence, said trade could pick up quickly.
"We could see some significant price appreciation this week and going forward for the rest of September," he said, adding that new institutional money had been placed last week.
"People can't use Yeltsin's health as an excuse for not investing forever. He's not in the best of health, but he is operational," and the Chechnya conflict appears to be coming to a close, he said.
But Troika-Dialog salesman Herman Zvezdin, who said Russian commercial banks are showing interest in equities, said the new investment would keep to a trickle.

"The institutional elephants are waiting for a more civilised market. Some of them are taking on exposure in Russia to get the feeling for how it works, but there will be no major pickup unless there are significant (infrastructural) changes."
He predicted a gradual pickup in market steam, especially in preferred stocks, where a new market has formed, he said.
